From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

It has been revealed that united travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

According to recent reports, andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

Diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

In a recent development, forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Industry observers note that few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

With a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

In a recent development, juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

Pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the upcoming head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

Sources indicate that according to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

Sources indicate that the Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

Recent findings suggest that dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

The defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical strategy was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

Nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

United return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the concerns exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

Pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

For Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails.
  • It has been revealed that he needn’t have worried.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

It has been revealed that he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

According to recent reports, it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

In a recent development, “It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

According to recent reports, any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

In a recent development, “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Sources indicate that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

In a recent development, cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Industry observers note that alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Recent findings suggest that “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola remarked, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

“Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose noted. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola mentioned: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that demonstrated why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

In a recent development, his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has remarked and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

Sources indicate that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has mentioned that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He said: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola stated: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most notable one right now that we need to go there and win.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Recent findings suggest that liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with captain Bruno Fernandes among those questioning the decision.

The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak outside the penalty area. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

According to Sky Sports, United intend to challenge the decision, with Isak’s chances of regaining possession central to the dispute. Mauricio Pochettino questioned whether Isak would have reached the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, a view shared by midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”.

“To make a mistake like this can change a game,” he said, as reported by the Press Association. The Portuguese midfielder nevertheless accepted that United were responsible for conceding from the subsequent free-kick.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher offered a different assessment on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch programme, supporting Barrott’s decision while acknowledging the uncertainty over whether Isak would have reached the ball before Lammens.

“I think most people would have expected a red card,” Gallagher mentioned.

An attacker’s likelihood of retaining or regaining possession is among the factors referees must consider when assessing whether a foul has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that united host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Pochettino’s first home match in charge. Unless the appeal succeeds, Yoro will serve a one-match suspension against the Bees. United sit 19th in the Premier League, having won just one of their opening 11 matches. Yoro remains eligible for Wednesday’s Champions League fixture against Sporting, before attention turns to a crucial domestic fixture for Pochettino’s side.

It has been revealed that after the full-time whistle, Rabiot spoke alongside Ramos to both Sky and DAZN, offering his thoughts on what was a very successful evening in front of all the fans at San Siro. His words are via MilanNews.

Are you starting to build a good identity?

Sources indicate that “Our problem is that we have to be focused for 90 minutes. We did well today, even though we conceded a bit at the end, but that’s normal. As I said, we’re growing as a team: the quality of our play, the team spirit, the sacrifice for 90 minutes, and everyone.

“Gonçalo is the first to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us, and we have a lot of games: I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit. But everyone’s attitude was great today, and we have to keep it up.

In a recent development, “In these last few games, when we play like this, when we’re so focused and manage to do what we work towards in training, I think we’re all enjoying ourselves, even tonight. We created a lot, we scored a lot of goals. What we have to focus on is enjoying playing together.”.

Why didn’t you shoot before the first goal?

Sources indicate that “I wanted Pulisic to score, but the defender came back quickly. It’s true that I could have shot, but I get more pleasure from providing an assist than from scoring. But I did the assist afterwards.”.

In a recent development, “He does a great job. Not everyone understands it, but he does an incredible job. When we get in and score, it’s also credit to us. Then we feel happy when he scores, also because it gives him confidence. Good for us and for him, for everyone.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.
  • The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.
  • Industry observers note that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Industry observers note that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino stated.

“Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”.

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

Industry observers note that “But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

The FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

#130861. Latest Update: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations

Latest Update: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (474 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

Industry News: Ex-Man United star Gordon Strachan tells Mauricio Pochettino what will get the Red Devils out of current crisis

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester United need to show character as they attempt to bounce back in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, ex-Red Devils midfielder Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole.
  • The 20-time English champions will enter the European fixture with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:31.

Manchester United need to show character as they attempt to bounce back in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, ex-Red Devils midfielder Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The 20-time English champions will enter the European fixture with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.

Mauricio Pochettino will now take charge of his first European match for Man United, and there is pressure on the Argentine following the four-goal mauling at Anfield.

When asked whether the Sporting match provided Man United with the perfect chance to bounce back from the defeat to Liverpool, Strachan insisted that the players need to show character and heart in a bid to turn the club's campaign around.

"Well, to be fair, Liverpool should never really be a big ask for Man United as such, because the record there is terrific over the years. I mean, it's always been decent. That fixture is one of the ones that Liverpool really want to win because they know how dangerous Man United are," said Strachan.

"But it wasn't a real game after the first two goals, there was the sending-off, you know. And even the free kick, you think, right, if you see the free kick off, we can reorganise and organise with 10 players. We never even had time to do that. So, as a manager, you can't count that, you've just got to count that as a no-game.

Industry observers note that "But what you can do in that situation is ask, who kept pressing? Who do I want in my team? Because in adversity, you see the real character coming out, and in adversity in massive games, you see the real character. And it's not on your social media, it's not saying to the fans, we love you and we're sorry and all the rest of it. Don't apologise to me, just do something about it.

"Don't come in and hold your hand up and say, I'm sorry, gaffer. Don't apologise to me because I'm not interested in you telling me you're sorry for making a mistake. Just don't make a mistake. And if you do make a mistake, rectify it as swiftly as possible.

In a recent development, "What I'm talking about is managers will try and sort it out. Invariably, unless you can do something about it, physically or mentally, then it will appear again. They will appear, and they'll appear in crisis moments.

"As I stated, your character is shown up in crisis times and the same mistakes will be made by the same people whoever they play. And some people are just not good enough to play at this level.

In a recent development, "You know, we all talk about shapes and systems and this and that. The funny thing is, I don't think there's too many people talking about systems now. I think most people are now talking about, even if you talk with a bright manager, they talk about putting people under pressure, winning knockdowns, getting to the ball first, getting the ball to your front men.

"So, the system thing has kind of changed now. The only one that kind of really changes, it's gone from a back four to a back three, but the rest, like Brighton, Liverpool, Bournemouth, they're all playing the same sort of way.

In a recent development, "It's a kind of 4-2-3-1, where the four players up front are attacking players, whatever way you want to use it, two wide men, just off the front. Wales were the same with Craig Bellamy.

"So, I think that people are moving to that in general now, but there's not too much talking about systems now. It's more about closing down, getting to knockdowns, winning headers and free kicks and corner kicks.".

Man United have six points to show from their two matches in the league stage of this season's Champions League.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

  • The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the matter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:28 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 23 November 2026.

Celtic have accepted a reduced ticket allocation for their upcoming visit to Tynecastle despite calls from fans to reject the offer.

The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the matter.

Celtic will receive 508 tickets for the Premiership encounter on November 29, which will be their first visit to Tynecastle since beating Hearts to the title in the final stages of last season, a victory which resulted in a pitch invasion from some of their fans at Celtic Park.

A Celtic statement read: 'As supporters will know, our allocation for our forthcoming match against Heart of Midlothian at Tynecastle Stadium has been cut by 20 per cent, compared to our previous visit.

'There have been a variety of views expressed to the club from supporters in relation to accepting this allocation. Some groups representing travelling supporters explained to the club that their members did not wish to accept the tickets because of the reduced allocation.

'We have taken that into consideration and also raised their concerns with the home club, who have assured us that they have spoken to Police Scotland.

Hearts had stated that only 508 tickets will be made available for Celtic fans on November 29.

'Having carefully considered all of the circumstances, we can confirm we will accept the allocation of 508 tickets.

'We respect all views and opinions on this matter, and while we are concerned and disappointed at this reduction, and others across recent years, we feel it is important that the team has the backing of our fans within the stadium for an important match.

'We realise the difficulties such a reduction can cause and in light of our discussions with supporters, we can confirm that should any supporter who is successful in the ballot, but does not wish to accept this ticket, then this will NOT affect the away ticket record moving forward.

'We thank our fans for their continued support and can confirm that we will be discussing the matter further with both the home club and the SPFL.'.

Celtic and Rangers formerly received the full Roseburn Stand for their supporters at Tynecastle, which resulted in an allocation of almost 3,500 tickets.

However, that figure was reduced to about 1,250 tickets in the 2021-22 season amid increased demand from home fans after the lockdown, and was further cut by about half.

Only Hibernian now get the full Roseburn Stand in a reciprocal agreement between the Edinburgh rivals.

Tynecastle has a capacity of about 20,000 but Hearts’ attendances are normally around 18,700 as a number of seats are not in use to create a barrier between the home and away fans.

Visiting clubs get about 800 tickets for games at Celtic Park, which has a 60,000 capacity.

Recent findings suggest that for Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

According to recent reports, that number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F.

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the key detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Recent findings suggest that gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Sources indicate that alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

Recent findings suggest that that is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

Industry observers note that the Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive looks, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

Sources indicate that one is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

The other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

The complication is Reece James. The captain’s fitness issues, including his current England hamstring concern, mean Chelsea still need genuine right-sided depth.

It has been revealed that palestra may be part of the future, but Gusto is already part of the present. Chelsea have too often needed emergency solutions in that area to treat proven depth lightly.

That is why Read Chelsea’s recent look at James awaiting hamstring scan results matters in this debate. Right-back remains one of the most talented areas of the squad, but also one of the least straightforward.

This is why Gusto’s France rhythm is more valuable than a simple tournament diary entry. Chelsea are watching a player operate inside an elite international camp, learn from a club legend and handle a public transfer valuation that can change his status overnight.

Alonso’s first decision does not have to be final, but it does have to be clear.

If Gusto stays, he needs a defined role early in pre-season and a pathway that makes sense alongside Palestra and James. If Chelsea sell, they need to do it at a number that justifies weakening one of the few squad areas where youth, speed and top-level experience already overlap.

Gusto’s Kante lesson, then, is not just a feel-good Chelsea connection. It is a reminder of the standard Alonso must demand before deciding whether £75million is a price to accept or a warning sign that Chelsea should hold firm.

Mauricio Pochettino praised Manchester United’s character and spirit after his side earned a 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Manchester United travelled to Portugal looking to respond after their disappointing 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first game in charge. They showed a much-improved performance away from home, although a number of costly moments prevented the upcoming head coach from celebrating his first victory.

Bruno Fernandes scored twice on his return to the stadium, putting United ahead after Luis Suarez had given Sporting the lead. The home striker also scored twice, including a penalty, to ensure the points were shared.

In a recent development, senne Lammens had earlier saved a Suarez spot-kick, but the United goalkeeper was involved in another penalty incident that allowed the Sporting forward to find the net. United also had two goals ruled out, while Youri Tielemans was sent off late in the contest.

Despite the frustrating outcome, Pochettino was pleased with what he saw from his players.

The Argentine felt United controlled large periods of the first half but were disappointed to go into the break behind.

“The first half I think we controlled the game, I think we dominated. We were disappointed to finish the first half 1-0 down,” Pochettino stated after the game.

“The second half I think we started the way we want to play. That is the style, the character. That is the way we want to establish and feeling this way we can perform.”.

The United boss also made it clear that he was proud of the players despite the decisions and incidents that went against them.

According to recent reports, “I’m so proud of my players. I think it was a very tough game. I liked the team during 90 minutes, in the way that we demonstrated personality and character.”.

Pochettino felt his side had been punished repeatedly in key moments.

“In the second half, we recovered a lot of balls in the opposite half. We were aggressive and I think that is the way we want to play,” he added.

In a recent development, after the heavy defeat at Anfield, United showed a different level of fight in Lisbon. The draw will still feel like a missed opportunity for Manchester United and Pochettino. However, the Argentine manager believes his players are beginning to embrace the style of play he wants.

By Freddie Cotton | 24 Nov 2026 20:48, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:58.

Marseille welcome Levski Sofia to the Stade Velodrome on Thursday evening on matchday five of the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, Les Olympiens claimed a crucial 1-0 win away to Bayer Leverkusen, while the Blues beat Polish side Jagiellonia by the same scoreline at the National Stadium Vasil Levski.

After narrowly missing out on booking their place in the UEFA Champions League for the second consecutive year last season, finishing fifth in Ligue 1 and just one point below Lyon in fourth, Marseille will be extremely disappointed with how they have performed on the continent so far this campaign.

Although they edged out Leverkusen in their latest Europa League fixture, losses to Sturm Graz, Olympiacos and Besiktas in each of their opening three matches mean Bruno Genesio’s men have earned just three points so far in Europe, leaving them 31st in the league phase table and outside of the knockout stage places.

Despite conceding two late goals to lose against Le Mans on Sunday evening, Les Olympiens have seen a huge improvement in their league endeavours, having won each of their prior five matches to right now sit fifth in the Ligue 1 table and just three points outside the automatic Champions League qualification places.

Marseille are yet to claim victory over Levski, though they do boast a mainly positive record against Bulgarian opposition, having beaten CSKA Sofia in each of their other two meetings with efbet League sides.

Having won their first efbet League title since 2009 last season and finished 10 points ahead of runners-up Ludogorets, who had triumphed in each of the previous 14 consecutive campaigns, Levski competed in the qualifying stages of the Champions League for the first time in 17 years during the summer.

The Blues impressed in their efforts for tournament qualification, beating Borac Banja Luka, Univ Craiova and Kairat Almaty to progress to the decisive playoff tie, but having endured a 4-0 aggregate defeat against Greek giants AEK Athens, the Bulgarian side are instead competing in the Europa League this season.

However, Julio Velazquez’s men have given a good account of themselves so far on the continent as after taking just one point from their first two matches, Levski have won back-to-back matches in the Europa League to sit 10th in the standings with seven points and only outside the round-of-16 positions on goal difference.

While the Blues do not have the best recent record against French opposition, having won just one of their previous four meetings with Ligue 1 sides, that triumph did come over Marseille, with Levski securing a 1-0 win over Les Olympiens in the group stages of this competition in December 2005, when it was branded as the UEFA Cup.

On a more positive note, after missing the match against Leverkusen as a precaution, Moroccan forward Amine Harit has started Les Olympiens’ previous two league fixtures and looks set to return to feature from the off in the week too.

Netting eight Ligue 1 goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous four outings, Algerian forward Amine Gouiri is undoubtedly the hosts’ biggest threat going forward and will be hoping to add to his winner against Leverkusen last time out in the competition.

Having been left out of Levski’s Europa League squad list, Oliver Kamdem, Mustapha Sangare and Petko Hristov are all unavailable for Thursday’s fixture, while 34-year-old striker Radoslav Kirilov remains out with a knee glitch.

De Lange; Bezahaf, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Hojbjerg; Weah, Kondogbia, Abdelli, Paixao; Gouiri.

Vutsov; Neves, Dimitrov, Makoun, Maicon; Sergingo, Grujic, Moubarik; Soula, Reinaldo, Everton Bala.

While Levski have made a promising start to their campaign, we think Les Olympiens will bag all three points at the Stade Velodrome this week and are backing them to mount a late charge for a top-eight finish in the league phase.

In a recent development, sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

It has been revealed that on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

According to recent reports, "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

Sources indicate that that still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

According to recent reports, it is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

Industry observers note that the goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It has been revealed that but, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. Might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

Sources indicate that I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Recent findings suggest that michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

Industry observers note that I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

We wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a massive team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Sources indicate that now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so vital for us.

Industry observers note that there were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

Recent findings suggest that in the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

It has been revealed that I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

Industry observers note that it was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

Michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊.

The script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a significant impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager stated.

It has been revealed that “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

“But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty massive one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

It has been revealed that the mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and latest head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino was left frustrated by several refereeing decisions during Manchester United’s 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon, insisting his side were punished in key moments of the game.
  • Manchester United had to settle for a point in Portugal after a chaotic evening away from home.
  • Referee Szymon Marciniak came under scrutiny for a series of controversial decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino was left frustrated by several refereeing decisions during Manchester United’s 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon, insisting his side were punished in key moments of the game.

Manchester United had to settle for a point in Portugal after a chaotic evening away from home. Bruno Fernandes scored twice, but Luis Suarez also found the net on two occasions to deny Pochettino his first win as United head coach.

Referee Szymon Marciniak came under scrutiny for a series of controversial decisions. He ruled out an Amad Diallo goal after penalising Youri Tielemans for a foul in the build-up, blowing his whistle before the ball crossed the line. That meant VAR could not intervene on the goal and it was not given.

In a recent development, the Polish official also awarded Sporting a first-half penalty and disallowed what would have been a late United winner. He blew whistle on Patrick Dorgu for pushing goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, disallowing the goal.

Pochettino did not hide his frustration when asked about the decisions after the match.

“I think your first question is difficult to answer because I think everyone knows all that was, it was impossible,” he noted after the game.

“You know, it’s difficult to understand why that happened on the field. It’s difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions.”.

United also conceded an 80th-minute equaliser after Senne Lammens failed to hold a cross, allowing Suarez to score from close range.

However, Pochettino was keen to defend his goalkeeper rather than blame him for the mistake.

“I think, please, it’s to blame us,” the United boss remarked.

He acknowledged that his side needed to manage such situations better.

“But of course, we need to accept, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve, you know, the small details that for sure we will improve.”.

Pochettino’s frustration was understandable after two similar incidents of bad refereeing in his first two games at United. Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool was later overturned on appeal, while a series of errors against Sporting cost him yet another victory. But despite the errors, Pochettino also recognises that his players need to improve their decision-making during games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michael Olise has moved from former Chelsea academy footnote to genuine Ballon d’Or conversation piece.

That should land at Cobham as more than a wistful what-if.

Bavarian Football Works relayed comments from former Chelsea and France winger Florent Malouda, who described the Bayern Munich forward as a live Ballon d’Or contender if France turn their World Cup run into silverware.

The point is not simply that Chelsea once had Olise in the building. It is that his rise provides a hard benchmark for the type of final-third specialist Xabi Alonso must either develop or buy.

Chelsea have spent heavily on attacking upside. Olise’s rise is a reminder that the real separator is not potential, but repeatable elite production.

Bayern’s own season review underlines why the conversation has accelerated.

The German champions confirmed Olise finished 2025/26 with 25 goals and 28 assists from 57 competitive appearances. He was also named Bayern’s Player of the Season for a second straight year, finishing ahead of Harry Kane and Luis Diaz in the fan vote.

That is elite production from a wide creator who does not play like a chalk-on-boots winger.

In a recent development, olise can receive wide, drift inside, manipulate the half-space and still deliver the last pass at match-winning speed. Chelsea have bought attackers with pieces of that profile, but few have joined the dots with that level of consistency.

There is an obvious recruitment lesson here.

The market will now price that blend of creativity, ball security and goal threat close to superstar territory. If Chelsea want an Alonso attack that controls games rather than simply runs through them, the next winger decision cannot be judged on pace or upside alone.

It has to be judged on game control, final-third calm and repeat output.

The World Cup has sharpened the comparison.

Sources indicate that chelsea’s official France preview noted that Malo Gusto was in the same squad as N’Golo Kante and former Blues academy player Olise. It was a neat reminder of how many Chelsea strands sit inside Didier Deschamps’ group.

Bundesliga’s tournament analysis was even more revealing. It noted that Olise had reached 10 France goal involvements in 18 appearances and was named Player of the Match on his World Cup debut against Senegal.

Recent findings suggest that that same analysis highlighted the tactical adjustment that moved Olise closer to Kylian Mbappe after half-time. His passing range then became the lever that changed the game.

Recent findings suggest that that matters for Chelsea because Alonso’s best Bayer Leverkusen sides were built around players who could receive between lines without killing the tempo. Cole Palmer already gives Chelsea one version of that.

The wider question is whether the squad has another attacker who can bend matches from the opposite side without turning every possession into a one-v-one.

Olise’s Chelsea connection can easily become sentimental. The sharper editorial point is structural.

In a recent development, this is the calibre of player who once passed through the academy pathway and later became a global-level attacker elsewhere. Chelsea cannot change that history, but they can use it to stress-test the next wave of decisions.

That matters for Tyrique George, Kendry Paez, Estevao and any upcoming wide signing.

Recent findings suggest that readChelsea has already looked at how Tyrique George’s likely Everton return gives Alonso a fresh winger audit. Olise’s current standing raises the standard of that discussion.

In a recent development, he is no longer just a former academy name or a missed Premier League target. He is evidence of what happens when technical security, role clarity and patience meet elite coaching.

For Alonso, that is the real value of the Olise noise.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea do not need to turn every academy exit into regret. They do need to recognise the standard now being set by one of Cobham’s former pupils.

The next wide forward who gets serious minutes at Stamford Bridge has to be assessed against that ceiling, not against the safer language of potential.

AC Milan put in one of their best performances under Ruben Amorim so far to sweep aside Frosinone at San Siro.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report by writing that Lazio, Roma and Juventus also had fun this weekend, scoring a flurry of goals in their victories, but it is Milan that might just come away from the round 12 feeling best.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that within 20 minutes, the Rossoneri had already blown the game wide open, eventually putting five past their opponents. All of them were spectacular, lightning-fast, and following the same pattern: every single one a counter-attack.

Sources indicate that it was a throwback style of football, yet infused with the visionary approach of Amorim, making it both fresh and truly beautiful to watch. There may not be official statistics on this, but conceding from five lethal transitions feels like a record as Frosinone’s strategy certainly went beyond mere self-sabotage.

Sources indicate that yet, on days like this, this Milan – an enigma to its opponents, with fluid movement and interchangeable positioning – are a truly daunting prospect. When Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Luka Modrić and others perform at such a high level, we see the potential of this side.

In a recent development, the Diavolo have secured five wins in their last six league matches, yet in Europe, they have suffered three defeats in four games. Will Thursday’s clash against Olympiacos help restore the balance?

Industry observers note that there was nothing balanced about the game between Milan and Frosinone. It is true that Alvini’s incredibly bold (perhaps even reckless) side tried to go toe-to-toe with their opponents for an hour by attacking, playing long balls, and taking on defenders.

Recent findings suggest that yet, beyond this emphasis on a specific style of play, one could make more concrete assessments. The coach clearly understood how vital Raimondo is to a team featuring such direct and creative wingers, Ghedjemis on the right and Kvernadze (who was rather ineffective yesterday) on the left.

Raimondo was the perfect focal point for them and without him, things had already gone poorly against Cagliari. Alvini attempted to make adjustments but got it wrong: he abandoned his 4-2-3-1 formation in favour of a back three (Calvani, Monterisi, Cittadini).

It has been revealed that all this was undermined by a senseless tendency to push too high, maintaining a defensive line 57 metres from their own goal within a 3-4-3 setup that lacked a true striker, opting instead for a ‘false’ one in Schmid. Every time they lost possession, it resulted in a counter-attack and often a goal.

In a recent development, it might seem odd to start with Frosinone rather than the brilliance of Milan, but there’s no denying that the visitors played their part in the spectacle. This is a match that future opponents will need to study in minute detail, because Milan on the counter are a goal-scoring machine.

Amorim, too, has a knack for springing surprises, though as always the guessing game regarding his actual tactical setup for the day begins the moment the whistle blows. For example, it was not a back four as it appeared on paper.

Instead, the system actually gradually morphed into a 3-5-2, with Rabiot operating as a highly advanced right-sided central midfielder, almost an attacking midfielder. The key lies in the connection between the Frenchman and the stratospheric Moreira, who surged down the centre often.

In a recent development, keeping everything running at full throttle was the incredible playmaking of Modrić, who also serves as the team’s primary ball-winner. So much for being a ‘pensioner’.

Milan proved flawless in exploiting both structural weaknesses and individual errors. Frosinone’s DNA is defined by a headlong, aggressive approach, but the opening goal – stemming from a sequence on the right flank involving Modrić and Rabiot – ended up as an own goal by Calvani.

Recent findings suggest that just four minutes in, and the match was effectively decided. While Frosinone usually thrive on quick, darting attacks, here the roles were reversed. Another full-pitch surge, initiated by Ramos winning the ball from Calvani and carried forward by Moreira and Rabiot, left the Portuguese player unmarked to make it 2-0.

Only a reckless back pass from Musah gifted Masini a goal to pull it back to 2-1. In the second half, however, Amorim addressed the one area that looked shaky: he withdrew Bartesaghi – who had been struggling against Ghedjemis – shifting Musah to full-back and pairing Jashari with Modrić.

According to recent reports, it paid off immediately: Jashari broke away and fired home the 3-1 following yet another rapid transition. And that wasn’t the only one: Pulisic surged clear on his own after a Frosinone corner (4-1), and Cissé, having just come on, joined the fray at full throttle to add the fifth (5-1).

There were many top performances. Rabiot is like a freight train and deserved a goal. He had to settle for three assists (bringing his total to seven). Moreira is versatile, playing as a wing-back, a central midfielder, or a winger, much like he did for Belgium when they caused Italy so much trouble.

Recent findings suggest that ramos also moved well outside of his goal. Cissé was an absolute handful: he came on and scorrd, playing as a striker after the Portuguese felt a tweak. He did so with an effortless grace that makes him impossible for his markers to handle.

The end result is that Milan are back in fourth. The competition is fierce, but the Rossoneri are right there in the mix, and eventually, some of the others will stumble. Take Inter, for example. Frosinone need to rethink their strategy while waiting for the return of Raimondo.

Sources indicate that they’ve overachieved so far, but now they might need to be a bit more prudent. And what about Milan? If they don’t turn their trip to Athens into a Greek tragedy, perhaps their European campaign can get back on track, too.

According to recent reports, chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

It has been revealed that reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

Recent findings suggest that the Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

Industry observers note that this matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

According to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

In a recent development, “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

That statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

In a recent development, data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Sources indicate that within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

In a recent development, prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

Sources indicate that for Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a substantial boost. It could help fund latest signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

Industry observers note that city chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

Chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

The Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has refused to confirm whether Luke Shaw will be involved in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon.

Shaw has made the trip to Portugal alongside his teammates, having recovered from the muscular problem that has sidelined him since the early stages of October.

The 31-year-old has been a huge miss at the back for Man United, and Pochettino has welcomed the Englishman's return to fitness.

However, it remains to be seen whether he is involved against Sporting.

“All the players need to feel they can have an impact for the team and they can perform," Pochettino told reporters during his pre-game press conference.

“It’s up to us to give the opportunities to every single player in the moment that we believe that they deserve to be involved in the game.

“Of course, I know Luke from the past, in our time in Southampton, but all [of us who are] involved, we are not the same people now. It’s more than 10 years ago.

“Obviously, it’s good to see him and he came from a small issue but now he needs to recover his best form.

“It’s good to have him, because he’s experienced everything with the squad, but we’ll see if he can be involved tomorrow or not, from the beginning or during the game.”.

Matheus Cunha is suspended for the match following his red card against Roma in the team's last European fixture, while Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte are all injured for the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino also insisted during his press conference that Man United are 'not a fragile team' despite their huge difficulties this season.

The Red Devils will enter the game with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, and they at the moment sit down in 19th spot in the Premier League table.

"We are not fragile, we are a strong team who last season finished third. Sometimes things happen in football for different reasons. We need to identify why and we are working on it. I think we are going to turn the situation around," said the head coach.

Man United have two wins and two draws from their four matches in this season's Champions League, beating Sabah and Roma either side of defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como.
